reality_check.current_diagnosis: You can write a few pandas one‑liners and have watched countless "build a model in 5 minutes" videos, but you have never shipped code, never written a README, and you cannot explain why a model fails beyond "it overfits". Your biggest delusion is that copying a Kaggle notebook equals production‑grade skill.
reality_check.achievable_in_timeframe: A complete, version‑controlled end‑to‑end ML project (data ingest → model → API) that you can demo, plus a portfolio of 3‑4 solid GitHub repos with tests, Dockerfiles, and performance logs.
reality_check.unachievable_in_timeframe: Claiming you can design a distributed feature store, run real‑time inference at 10k QPS, or lead a team of senior engineers. Those are multi‑year, enterprise‑scale responsibilities.

strict_rules: No project without README and error analysis
Every commit must be atomic and include a descriptive message
All code must be linted (flake8) and type‑checked (mypy) before push

phases.title: Core Foundations & Tooling
phases.main_theme: Discipline, execution mechanics, and zero‑bullshit coding
phases.what_not_to_waste_time_on: Watching "Python for Data Science" playlists without coding, endless UI tutorials for Jupyter, and deep‑dive into every new Python library you see on Reddit.
key_topics: Automated testing (pytest) and CI basics (GitHub Actions)

checklist.text: Create a GitHub repo, enable branch protection, and push daily commits for 30 days (>=20 commits total)
Write a CLI tool that reads a CSV, prints basic stats, and handles malformed rows gracefully
Add unit tests covering 90% of the CLI logic using pytest
Containerize the CLI with a Dockerfile that builds in <2 minutes and runs without root
Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that lints, type‑checks, and runs tests on every PR
Write a 500‑word README + error‑analysis section describing what failed on malformed CSVs and how you fixed it

capstone_project.name: Data Ingestion Pipeline
capstone_project.problem: Ingest raw order CSVs from a mock food‑delivery partner, clean, validate, and store them in a SQLite DB for downstream analytics
capstone_project.deliverable: GitHub repo with: src/, tests/, Dockerfile, .github/workflows/, README (incl. usage, error analysis, performance numbers)
capstone_project.resume_bullet: Engineered a production‑grade CSV ingestion pipeline (Docker + CI) that validated 1M+ rows with 0% data‑loss, reducing manual cleaning time by 80%

checkpoint_rubric.on_track_if: ≥20 atomic commits, CI passes on every push, and you can explain each file in <60 seconds
checkpoint_rubric.falling_behind_if: Only watching videos, copying code without tests, or CI repeatedly failing

phases.drill_topic: Git branching strategies and rebasing vs merging

phases.title: Core Machine Learning Foundations
phases.main_theme: From toy models to reproducible experiments
phases.what_not_to_waste_time_on: Kaggle competitions that hide the data pipeline, endless hyperparameter‑grid tutorials without evaluation, and re‑implementing every scikit‑learn algorithm from scratch.
key_topics: Supervised learning basics (linear regression, logistic regression, tree‑based models)

checklist.text: Implement linear regression from scratch (numpy) and compare loss with scikit‑learn's implementation
Create a reproducible scikit‑learn pipeline that ingests a CSV, performs one‑hot encoding, scaling, and trains a GradientBoostingClassifier
Write unit tests for each custom transformer (edge cases, missing values)
Generate a full experiment report (markdown) with train/val/test splits, ROC‑AUC, confusion matrix, and a 200‑word error analysis
Store the trained model with joblib and write a small CLI to load + predict on a new CSV
Write a SQL query that extracts a feature (e.g., average order value per user) and integrate it into the pipeline

capstone_project.name: Customer Churn Prediction
capstone_project.problem: Predict whether a user will churn within 30 days using a synthetic Swiggy order history dataset
capstone_project.deliverable: GitHub repo with data/, src/, notebooks/, tests/, model/, README (incl. data schema, feature list, evaluation, error analysis)
capstone_project.resume_bullet: Built a churn‑prediction model (GradientBoosting, ROC‑AUC 0.87) and delivered a CLI + Dockerized inference service that scored 10k records in <30s

checkpoint_rubric.on_track_if: All pipeline components have tests, experiment report is reproducible, and you can explain why each feature was kept/removed in <2 minutes
checkpoint_rubric.falling_behind_if: Skipping tests, using default scikit‑learn pipelines without understanding, or reporting only accuracy

phases.title: Deep Learning & PyTorch Mastery
phases.what_not_to_waste_time_on: Re‑watching the same 10‑minute tutorial for every architecture, building GANs without understanding loss functions, and using every new PyTorch Lightning feature without a concrete need.
key_topics: CNNs for image data, transfer learning (ResNet, EfficientNet)
RNNs/Transformers for sequence data (optional but useful)
Experiment tracking (TensorBoard, Weights & Biases) and reproducibility

checklist.text: Implement a fully manual training loop for MNIST (no torch.nn.Module shortcut) and log loss/accuracy to TensorBoard
Fine‑tune a pretrained ResNet‑50 on a 2k‑image subset of a Swiggy menu dataset, achieving >80% top‑1 accuracy
Write unit tests for custom data augmentations and verify deterministic behavior with a fixed seed
Profile GPU memory usage, implement gradient checkpointing to fit a larger batch, and document the trade‑off
